messages:
alex_cs: FYI — Customer reported signup went fine, PayPal checkout completed but free-trial credits never showed up. Account acct_0A9f, email: forwarded+acme@examplecorp.com. They verified email after a delay (forwarding), but our autogrant never fired. Ticket CS-4219 opened. Can payments/eng triage and manual-grant?

support-bot: Ticket CS-4219 created: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/CS-4219 — assigned to payments. Added logs + customer transcript.

jessica_payments: Thanks Alex — can you paste the PayPal txn id (or last 6) and the exact signup IP/time? Also whether they signed up via SSO or direct email flow. Need to check our post-checkout webhook processing and bin-country check.

alex_cs: Paste safe bits: txn: PP-8Z3X9K (customer gave this), signup IP 44.34.12.77 at 2026-03-12T15:22Z. They did NOT use SSO; used email signup then clicked verification link (email is forwarded alias) — customer says verification click arrived ~6m after initial signup. Steps they followed: 1) email + password 2) PayPal express checkout 3) get verification email (forwarded) 4) clicked verify link 6 minutes later -> account shows verified but no credits.

ow to reproduce locally:
```bash
# check credits for account
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acct_0A9f | jq .credits
# check payments webhook processing
curl -s -X GET https://payments.redwood.ai/webhooks/last?txn=PP-8Z3X9K
```

logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-12T15:22:01Z] account created acct_0A9f ip=44.34.12.77 locale=GB
[2026-03-12T15:22:05Z] external_payment_start txn=PP-8Z3X9K provider=paypal status=pending
[2026-03-12T15:24:30Z] email_verify_sent to=forwarded+acme@examplecorp.com
[2026-03-12T15:28:12Z] paypal_webhook_received txn=PP-8Z3X9K status=COMPLETED bin_country=IE
[2026-03-12T15:28:20Z] autogrant_pipeline skippable=true reason=region_gate_matched rule=bin_country:IE
```

own: Hmm — webhook shows bin_country=IE while account.locale=GB. Our autogrant routing currently blocks if payment bin country != account.locale and if verification came after webhook. That explains skip. Two issues: forwarded email verif delay (common) and bin-country mismatch from PayPal reporting IE for Irish-registered PayPal account, while user is UK.

owen_eng: Can we confirm the exact gating order? I think current logic is: 1) payment.completed -> run bin-country gating -> if passes and account.verified -> autogrant, else queue for verification event. There might be a race where payment arrives slightly before verification and bin-country mismatch triggers immediate skip rather than queued retry. Need trace.

lina_ops: Agreed — quick mitigation: manual grant, and change autopolicy to treat bin-country mismatch as non-fatal when account.locale present OR queue for post-verification retry for 30m. I can do manual grant now if payments approves.

jessica_payments: I ran a check on webhook processing and the payment was processed by our payments queue with bin_country=IE. Policy is strict by default for historical fraud cases, but we can make an exception. Manual grant + annotate ticket. Applying manual 1500-token trial credit now for acct_0A9f and marking payment record with note: "manual override: CS-4219 — bin-country mismatch + delayed email verification".

jessica_payments: Manual grant complete — 1500 tokens added, customer notified. I also removed the hard-fail for bin-country mismatch in the autogrant rule for 30m window and created an internal follow-up EPIC: PAY-742 to add a post-payment verification retry path.

alex_cs: Thanks all — customer confirmed credits visible. Please add a short KB blurb for CS reps on these multi-factor races (forwarded email delays + PayPal bin mismatches). Also FYI for product: consider preferring account.locale over payment.bin_country for autogrant.

owen_eng: Filing a small PR to change logic to: if payment.bin_country != account.locale then mark for manual-review OR retry on verification event within 30m rather than immediate skip. Link PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/autogrant/pulls/118

lina_ops: Noted, closing internal follow-up after PAY-742 triage.

alex_cs: Closing thread — customer happy. :tada:
